body:
incident-bot: Pager: model-quality-regression triggered for model: rwdx-large-v2 in us-west1 — severity: high. Metric: policy_eval_fail_rate > 8% (5m). @alice_oncall is paged.

alice_oncall: Ack — I’m on it. hopping into the canary logs now.

mike_sre: Seeing a spike in token-level perplexity on canary shards 3/4, also a 502 rate bump on the routing layer. Could be a tokenizer mismatch or new tokenizer weights.

tara_ml: Interesting — we rolled in tokenizer fix in the last deploy window (hash: 7f3a2e). That could cause misaligned embeddings → some rerank/eval failures.

alice_oncall: Good find. Can we quickly verify whether traffic still hitting the old tokenizer variant? run a quick query: `curl -s https://canary.metrics/api | jq '.deploys | map(select(.sha=="7f3a2e"))'`

mike_sre: Ran that. Output: one canary host still on previous sha (6b9c1d). There’s a partial rollout. Probable mismatch between model binary and tokenizer submodule.

josh_support: Any customer impact visible yet? I’ve got a high-priority ticket from a fintech customer reporting hallucinations & truncated outputs.

tara_ml: That matches the eval signatures — prompts with long system prefixes show truncated completions. We should stop the canary rollout and route traffic to last known-good model variant.

alice_oncall: Agreed. Action plan: 1) Pause canary rollout, 2) Bump traffic to pinned model `rwdx-large-v1` in us-west1, 3) Notify affected customers and post status page note, 4) Start rollback of tokenizer commit.

mike_sre: On it. Pausing rollout now. Command I used:```bash
# pause rollout
redwood deploy cancel --env us-west1 --campaign canary-7f3a2e
# re-route traffic
redwood route update --model rwdx-large-v1 --region us-west1 --percent 100
```

mike_sre: Rollout paused, traffic routed to v1. Monitoring for error drop.

alice_oncall: Monitoring dashboards — 502s down to baseline, perplexity falling. Good.

sophie_prodops: Drafting status page and customer note. Suggest short, empathetic wording: "We’re investigating degraded outputs for model rwdx-large-v2 in US-West. Traffic has been routed to a pinned stable model and we’re working on a fix; no further action required from customers." Want approval before posting.

josh_support: Thumbs up from Support — please include a note that customers can open a priority ticket if they see production correctness issues.

tara_ml: I’m spinning up a repro job against both tokenizer variants to confirm root cause; will capture diff and create a revert PR if confirmed. Repro command:```python
# repro harness
from rwd_eval import Runner
r = Runner("rwdx-large-v2", tokenizer_override=None)
r.run_suite("long-system-prefixes")
```

alice_oncall: Handoff note for next shift: paused canary, traffic pinned to `rwdx-large-v1` in us-west1, customers notified draft pending, ML is running repro & preparing PR. No data exfil.

mike_sre: Alerting infra team to watch autoscaler for spike while traffic shifts. Also capturing logs to /var/logs/canary-7f3a2e/*.gz and retained for 72h.

sophie_prodops: Posting status page update now: "Investigating degraded model outputs for rwdx-large-v2 in US-West. Traffic routed to a stable pinned variant; we are actively investigating impact and will update here. Estimated next update: 30 minutes." Posting.

josh_support: Posted customer-facing blurb in the support ticket as well. Providing customers the incident link.

tara_ml: Repro confirms tokenizer mismatch: token ID alignment differs after the tokenizer change which yields invalid attention masks for long prefixes. Creating revert PR and tagging @alice_oncall + @mike_sre for rollout approval.

alice_oncall: When PR ready, we will: stage on a single host, run smoke evals (quality + latency), then roll forward if green. If issues persist, we’ll keep pin until patch validated.

mike_sre: Patch deployment checklist (for the record): 1) apply revert to tokenizer submodule, 2) build model artifact, 3) stage on isolated canary host, 4) smoke eval suite <= 5% regression, 5) progressive rollout.

sophie_prodops: Customer comms update drafted: "We routed traffic to a stable model to limit impact. The issue originated from an internal tokenizer change in our recent deploy; we’re reverting and validating now. We will follow up when we have a confirmed fix and timeline." Approve?

josh_support: Approve. Add note offering direct follow-up to affected customers.

alice_oncall: Good. Finalizing internal postmortem template fields for when incident closes: root cause, timeline, remediation steps, customer list impacted, follow-ups (retro + QA gating). I’ll hand off to the next oncall at 2432110180.

incident-bot: Incident status update: mitigated — traffic pinned to stable variant; active remediation in progress. Incident channel will be archived after resolution.

alice_oncall: Leaving detailed logs & links in the incident doc (internal) and adding playbook updates to avoid partial canary rollouts with tokenizer changes. Thanks team. :thumbsup:
